Closing date: 13 November 2026

responsibilities:
Successful candidates will serve as functional police officials. As such, they will be deployed to carry out the following functions:
Prevent, combat and investigate crime
Maintain public order
Protect and secure the inhabitants of the Republic and their property
Uphold and enforce the law.
requirements:
A person who applies to be employed as an entry level police trainee must - Apply on the form determined by the National Commissioner and affirm under oath or by way of a solemn declaration that the particulars furnished in the application, are the truth and correct
Be a citizen of the Republic of South Africa of which documentary proof must be furnished
Be at least eighteen (18) years of age and not older than thirty-five (35) years of age at the time of the closing date for applications stipulated in the relevant advertisement, of which documentary proof must be furnished
Submit himself or herself to a physical and medical examination as determined by the National Commissioner and must be found to be physically, medically and mentally fit for appointment in the service
Undergo a psychological and integrity assessment as determined by the National Commissioner and be found to comply with the profile of a police official
Be in possession of a grade 12 school certificate or equivalent qualification of which documentary proof must be furnished
Be proficient in at least English and one other official language
Be prepared to take the oath of office
Be prepared to undergo such training as, where and when determined by the National Commissioner
Not have any tattoo marks which will be visible when wearing any uniform of the Service
Not have been declared unfit to possess a firearm
Not have any previous criminal convictions or any pending criminal cases
Not have been dismissed for serious misconduct from the employ of a previous employer, where such dismissal relates to any act of dishonesty or violence; sexual harassment or is drug related
Allow a buccal sample and his or her fingerprints to be taken and verified against the criminal record system
Allow background enquiries to be made
Be prepared to undergo security vetting and obtain the level of security clearance determined by the National Commissioner; and Be prepared to serve anywhere in the Republic.
Applicants in possession of a relevant three (3) years tertiary qualification (NQF 6 or higher) i.e. Criminal Law / Policing / Forensic investigation etc.
Applicants in possession of other three (3) years tertiary qualification (NQF 6 or higher
Applicants in possession of Grade 12 school certificate with the minimum requirements for admission to bachelor’s degree
All applicants will be subjected to a fitness, psychometric and integrity testing as well as medical evaluation and will be interviewed during the recruitment, selection and enlistment process. The SAPS will also verify the qualifications, drivers’ licence, where applicable, citizenship and residential address of each applicant.
Applicants will be subjected to a vetting process which will include security screening, reference checking, social media presence and fingerprint verification to establish whether any illicit activity has been recorded or is pending against candidates.
Applicants who previously served in a Government Department and who were dismissed because of misconduct will not be considered for appointment in the South African Police Service (SAPS).
In view of the physical demands of the Basic Police Development Learning Programme, applicants with chronic diseases, physical impairments or any other health condition that may lead to interruption of the training programme, may be excluded from participation in the programme. Should applicants fail to disclose any health condition it may result in their withdrawal from the programme on the determination thereof.

responsibilities:
Manage and enforce Road Traffic, Public Passenger, Transport Legislation and other relevant legislation.
Develop operational strategies and ensure implementation of approved traffic law enforcement strategies.
Ensure the free flow of traffic through point duty and traffic control at congested areas, coordinate activities, and safeguard accident scenes.

Coordinate execution of arrests on traffic-related matters, attend court proceedings, and give evidence.

Manage traffic policing projects.

Manage escorting of abnormal vehicles and loads to ensure safe movement thereof.

Manage the execution of joint law enforcement strategies and projects.
Evaluate and report on strategies and projects.

Implement innovations to improve the working environment and conduct visits to officers in the field.
Assist with the updating of the environmental analysis to ensure that it is used as a baseline for planning.
Perform basic management functions (planning, organizing, leading and control).
Conduct planning, feedback, evaluation, and information-sharing meetings with subordinates.
Assist with human resource issues at the station and coordinate staff quarterly performance appraisals.
Identify and manage risks:
Identify relevant risks
Develop a plan to address risks
Implement and monitor plan
Evaluate progress
Manage the performance of all administrative activities and related duties
Ensure that the motor vehicle fleet is managed properly
Monitor the state of equipment and assist with proactive replacement planning, including identifying and monitoring members involved in accidents.
Ensure effective loss control measures are in place to address loss of firearms and other related equipment and strive towards reducing the financial value of losses.
Participate in budget planning as required by the Center Manager.
Monitor monthly expenditure and inspection reports from the province and implement corrective action in problem areas.
Regular budget control and management discussions as part of management meetings and share information with members regarding the center's budget priorities.

A Basic Traffic Diploma.
6 - 10 years’ working experience in the field.

The incumbent is responsible for the effective management of soft services within the departmental property portfolio, and in that capacity conducts site visits and condition assessments to determine soft service requirements.
The incumbent ensures that all facilities are maintained at habitable and hygienic standards, fit for occupation and for the purposes for which they are used.
The incumbent manages the delivery of cleaning and hygiene services in compliance with contractual specifications, service level agreements, the Occupational Health and Safety Act, 1993 (Act 85 of 1993) and its regulations, and applicable public health requirements.
The incumbent also manages waste removal, grounds maintenance and gardening services in compliance with the National Environmental Management Act, 1998 (Act 107 of 1998), the National Environmental Management: Waste Act, 2008 (Act 59 of 2008) and applicable municipal by-laws, including the lawful handling, segregation, storage, removal and disposal of general and hazardous waste.
Pest control and fumigation programmes are implemented in accordance with approved schedules and applicable legislation, including the use of duly registered operators and approved products and the safe handling of hazardous chemical substances.
The incumbent maintains and updates project and facility information for all sites under the unit’s management.
The incumbent ensures that all equipment used by staff is in good functional, safe and serviceable condition, that statutory inspections and certification requirements are met, and that equipment is operated by competent persons.
Repairs are managed so that defects are attended to timeously and within approved budgets, with priority given to defects that compromise health, safety, hygiene or environmental compliance.
The incumbent plans and liaises with Supply Chain Management and Director Facilities Maintenance and for the timeous procurement of the consumables, supplies and spares required and service providers in compliance with the applicable procurement prescripts and with due regard to safety data requirements and environmentally responsible specifications.

The incumbent manages subordinates and maintains discipline in accordance with the applicable labour relations prescripts.

The incumbent promotes a safe working environment for staff and service providers’ employees in terms of the Occupational Health and Safety Act, 1993.

Finally, the incumbent manages the unit’s funds in compliance with the Public Finance Management Act, 1999 and the Treasury Regulations, and limits under-expenditure and over-expenditure in accordance with the departmental budget allocations.

about_role:
The Department of Infrastructure Development (Gauteng) is hiring a Boiler Operator in Maintenance, based in District Maintenance Hub Tshwane Mechanical Services. This is a permanent post, paying R201,093.

How to apply: To apply for the below position, please apply online at https://jobs.gauteng.gov.za
Reference number to quote: REFS/056866
Closing date: 09 November 2026
Use the new Z83 form and attach a detailed CV.
responsibilities:
Request chemicals from stores as required.
Test quality of water of softeners as well as the returning flows of condensate water.
Fill chemicals tank with required chemicals as prescribed.
Top up salt in brine tank.
Check working conditions of chemical pumps.
Test total dissolve solids (TDS) and blow-down according to prescripts.
Monitor the stream pressure constantly Check correct temperature of hot well tanks.
Adjust the stoker for efficient steam delivery.
Report all defects immediately.
Check the feed water pump-levels and hot well tanks for sufficient water supply to the boiler.
Ensure that standby boilers and funnel is full of water and chemicals at all times.
Control the flow of fuel.
Ensure that the boiler environment is well maintained.
Ensure proper usage of protective clothing.
Ensure that the boiler environment is clean and safe.
Ensure that the brine tank and water filter are cleaned as prescribed.
Ensure the removal of ash from boilers, gritt arrester and smoke box.
Log all recordings as per the assessment in the logbook.
Perform supervisory functions.
Receive and signoff on the delivery of coal.
Provide shift reports.
Maintenance of shift/overtime register.
Perform related adhoc duties.
requirements:
Grade 10 and an equivalent recognized National Steam Certificate.
At least 1 year appropriate hands-on experience gained in boiler operating.
Competencies:
Basic knowledge of norms and standards on low pressure
Knowledge of Maintenance Works Norms and Standards
Knowledge of maintenance tools
Knowledge of Occupational Health and Safety Act
Skills:
Interpersonal relations
Ability to utilise Public Works maintenance tools
Planning and organising
Staff supervision
Communication (written & verbal)
Attributes:
People centred
Professionalism
Collective responsibility
Transformation
Batho Pele Principles
Attention to detail
Honesty and integrity
Strong ethics

Insight into local healthcare delivery, diversity, transformation and equity.

The Master Installation Electrician is a person who has been registered as a Master Installation Electrician in terms of regulation 9 and who has been approved by the Chief Inspector for the verification and certification of the construction, testing and inspection of any electrical installation for efficient and effective custody, transfer and transport of petroleum products in liaison with Operations, Instrumentation and Mechanical departments in Transnet Pipelines. The Master Installation Electrician is responsible for electrical scheduling, inspection and to ensure safe working conditions.
responsibilities:
1) Managing of COC’s (Certificate of compliance) a. Undertake periodic inspections and issuing COC’s as per National Codes and OSH Act b. Conduct 2Y compulsory OHSact Hazardous area equipment inspections. c. Maintain depot COC’s and compliance of Electrical Equipment housed in Hazardous areas.
2) Give guidance and oversee Electrical Installation
3) Control the integrity of Equipment
Ensure the correct application of the correct Electrical equipment in the Plant/operations.
4) PREVENTATIVE MAINTENANCE
To perform preventative maintenance tasks on electrical equipment by detecting, repairing and reporting minor defects as well as reporting major defects thereby ensuring reliable equipment for the continuous operation of the pipeline e.g. 220V-3.3 Kv motors, control gear and trip protection equipment e.g Actuators.
5) DEFECT REPAIR
Identify, analyse and repair defects on installed (live) equipment. Repair specific installed (live) equipment by performing diagnostic tests to identify defects and effect repairs. Reading and understanding schematics and reports are essential e.g. Mainline motor starter and trip protection, 380V panel starters and trip protection.
6) BONDING
Witness and install
7) REMOVE AND REPLACE INSTALLED (LIVE) EQUIPMENT
Removal and replacement of specific equipment by planning the complete installation, isolation and removal of the equipment as well as preparing and installing the replacement, energising and testing the operations of the equipment e.g. Main motors, Actuators, lights, cranes, enclosures, isolators and stop/start stations.
8) REFURBISHMENT AND MODIFICATION ELECTRICAL EQUIPMENT Refurbishing equipment by disassembling the equipment, replacing defective parts, reassembling and testing the equipment to the manufacturers specification e.g.
Starters
Actuators
Certify all refurbished Equipment.
9) HIGH VOLTAGE EQUIPMENT Obtaining authorisation and undertaking switching (A-Brown) and earthing on high voltage switchgear and equipment up to 132KV, issuing of work and test permits as well as undertaking maintenance of the above equipment. Also supervise unathorised personnel in substations and HT yards Work to a clearance of live high voltage equipment as per electrical HIGH VOLTAGE instructions.
10) SAFETY
Attend Meetings
Do Safety Inspections
Use of safety equipment
Ensure compliance of Equipment for flameproof safety and standards
Assist with Job Observations and Supervision of personnel.
11) ADMIN The effective control of administration duties which includes: -
Reports (defect, inspection)
Obtain and cancel hot work permits (Electrical)
Job cards
Operate SAP Modules (MM & IM)
Maintain records, registers and COC’s as per applicable legislation
Assist with internal electrical audits.
Assist with Acting as an Electrical Supervisor as and when required.

about_role:
Heineken Beverages is hiring an Automation Engineer, based in Johannesburg.
The key purpose of this role is to provide structured, strategic and leadership within the automation and control discipline across Heineken Beverages manufacturing operations. The role develops and governs automation standards, architecture, frameworks and lifecycle practices; influences site and project decisions; improves manufacturing reliability and performance; strengthens PCD cybersecurity; and enables the controlled implementation and enhancement of digital manufacturing technologies. The role works across sites and functions to ensure automation solutions are safe, reliable, maintainable, secure, integrated, scalable and aligned with Heineken requirements and long-term business priorities.
responsibilities:
Automation Manufacturing Reliability and Continuous Improvement:
Provide cross-site technical leadership to improve the reliability, maintainability and performance of automation and control systems.
Establish and govern reliability standards, maintenance strategies and performance measures for PLC, SCADA, HMI, industrial networks, drives, instrumentation and associated control infrastructure.
Analyse systemic failures, repeat breakdowns and automation-related production losses; lead structured root cause analysis and ensure sustainable corrective and preventive actions are implemented.
Support sites with complex or high-impact automation incidents while strengthening site capability and ownership.
Identify and prioritise opportunities to improve throughput, quality, energy performance, process stability, OPI and cost through automation and advanced control.
Develop reusable troubleshooting practices, standard diagnostics, technical guidance and lessons-learned mechanisms across the manufacturing network.
Automation Projects and Obsolescence Management:
Provide technical assurance and lifecycle governance for automation capital projects, upgrades and obsolescence programmes.
Define automation project requirements, design principles, acceptance criteria and handover standards.
Review and approve control philosophies, functional design specifications, architectures, software designs, network designs and supplier proposals for compliance with approved standards.
Participate in design reviews, risk assessments, FAT, SAT, commissioning, performance verification and operational handover for strategic projects.
Develop and maintain automation asset lifecycle and obsolescence frameworks, site risk profiles, technology roadmaps and prioritised replacement plans.
Automation Technology, Architecture and Integration:
Define and govern fit-for-purpose automation technologies and integration patterns across the control and manufacturing landscape.
Own and maintain reference architectures, approved technology standards, software libraries, naming conventions, interface principles and engineering practices for automation and control systems.
Evaluate emerging and existing technologies against business value, cybersecurity, interoperability, supportability, scalability and lifecycle requirements.
Ensure reliable integration between field devices, control systems, SCADA, historians, MES, utilities platforms, reporting solutions and approved enterprise services.
Guide industrial communication and data integration using approved protocols, segmented architectures and clearly defined ownership boundaries between OT and IT.
Maintain strategic relationships with OEMs, system integrators and technology partners; influence roadmaps and ensure solutions remain aligned with Heineken architecture and support models.
Create governance mechanisms for deviations, technical decisions, solution assurance and controlled introduction of new technology.
PCD Cybersecurity and Compliance:
Strengthen cybersecurity and compliance within the Process Control Domain through standards, risk management and technical governance.
Translate Heineken PCD security requirements into practical automation engineering standards, implementation roadmaps and assurance controls.
Govern secure network segmentation, access control, remote access, backup and restore, patching, malware protection, account management, logging and recovery practices for automation assets.
Support PCD risk assessments, audits, vulnerability remediation and incident response, ensuring actions are prioritised according to operational and business risk.
Embed security-by-design into automation projects, system changes, supplier access and technology lifecycle decisions.
Define evidence, documentation and compliance routines required to demonstrate that controls are implemented, sustained and periodically tested.
Collaborate with PCD Security, IT, site engineering and external partners to resolve risks without compromising safety, quality or production continuity.
Digital Manufacturing Implementation and Enhancement:
Enable sustainable digital manufacturing solutions by ensuring robust automation data foundations, controlled integration and measurable operational value.
Provide automation leadership for historian, MES, OPI, energy, condition monitoring, analytics and other approved digital manufacturing initiatives.
Define data acquisition, contextualisation, tag, interface, time synchronisation, data quality and ownership standards from shop-floor systems to authorised digital platforms.
Ensure digital solutions are industrialised, supportable, cybersecure and integrated into site operating and maintenance routines rather than remaining isolated pilots.
Partner with operations, engineering, digital, data and IT teams to translate business problems into scalable automation and data solutions.
Assess solution performance after implementation and drive enhancements based on adoption, reliability, data quality and realised business benefits.
Standards, Governance, Capability and Strategic Influence:
Build a consistent and sustainable automation engineering capability across Heineken Beverages through governance, assurance and knowledge leadership.
Develop, maintain and deploy automation policies, standards, frameworks, specifications, templates and technical procedures aligned with global and local requirements.
Establish governance forums, compliance assessments, maturity reviews and performance reporting to provide visibility of automation risks, priorities and progress.
Influence investment plans and management decisions by presenting clear technical risk, lifecycle, cost and business-impact information.
Provide coaching, technical mentoring and structured capability development for site automation engineers, technicians, project engineers and relevant stakeholders.
Facilitate cross-site communities of practice, knowledge sharing, benchmarking and replication of proven solutions.
Define competency expectations and support succession and training for the automation and control discipline.
Act as a recognised subject matter expert and escalation point, balancing enterprise standardisation with site requirements and operational realities.
Safety, Health, Environment and Quality:
Ensure that automation strategies, designs, changes and work practices protect people, product, plant, information and the environment.
Apply management-of-change, functional safety, quality, environmental and legal requirements to automation engineering activities.
Ensure control system modifications are appropriately assessed, tested, approved, documented, backed up and recoverable before release to production.
Promote safe engineering behaviours and ensure suppliers and partners comply with site and Heineken SHE requirements.
requirements:
Bachelor’s Degree in Electrical Engineering, Electronic Engineering, Mechatronics, Process Control, Instrumentation, Automation or a related engineering discipline.
Relevant professional registration, postgraduate qualification or recognized automation, industrial networking, cybersecurity or project certification would be an added advantage.
Minimum 10 years relevant experience in industrial automation and control within a manufacturing or process environment, including experience with PLC, SCADA/HMI, industrial networks, drives, instrumentation and system integration.
Demonstrated experience in automation projects, reliability improvement, technology lifecycle or obsolescence management and cross-functional technical leadership.
Experience operating across multiple manufacturing sites, developing standards or providing technical governance at business, regional or Centre of Excellence level would be an added advantage.

Note: For re-advertised posts: Candidates who previously applied need to re-apply. Call for applications to serve as members of the correctional supervision and parole board. The Minister of Correctional Services in terms of Section 74 of the Correctional Services Act, Act 111 of 1998 invite interested and suitable candidates to apply for an opportunity to serve as members of the Correctional Supervision and Parole Board. The Parole Board is an independent body whose main aim is to protect the public by risk assessing offenders to decide whether they can be safely released into the community. The main role of a Chair (and Vice in the chairs absence) is decision making. Decision making in light of a number of factors, that is:- rights of the offender (as far as the right to be considered in light of relevant legislation), calculation of the minimum detention period, understanding of criminal justice value chain, court papers, sentencing remarks, copy of the judgment, copy of the warrant of detention, case law, SAP 69 and 62, understanding the various reports by the DCS professionals, understanding of the rehabilitation process, risk assessment, victim/community empathy, public safety etc. Applicants who have retired from the Public Service with a specific determination that they cannot be reappointed or have been declared medically unfit will not be considered. Term of office will be for a period of five (5) years or as may be determined by the Minister in line with Section 74 (7) of the Correctional Services Act, Act 111 of 1998. Applications: Applications must be submitted on the Z83 form (Public Service application form) accessible on the link below and must be completed in full. Only a detailed CV should be attached to your application form. Only shortlisted candidates will be required to submit certified copies not older than 6 months of qualifications and other related documents on or before the day of the interview. Applicants must note that further checks will be conducted once they are shortlisted and that their appointment is subject to positive outcomes on these checks, which include security clearance, security vetting, qualification verification and criminal records verification. Candidates must comply with the minimum appointment requirements. CV’s should be aligned to reflect one’s degree of compliance with the advertisement requirements and responsibilities. The Department of Correctional Services reserves the right not to fill these posts. Persons with disabilities are encouraged to apply. Candidates must comply with the minimum appointment requirements. CV’s should be aligned to reflect one’s degree of compliance with the advertisement requirements and responsibilities. The Department of Correctional Services reserves the right not to fill these posts.
responsibilities:
Analyse and critically evaluate information in order to identify continuing risk/dangerous-ness in an individual offender’s case, where information may come from a variety of sources including electronic and paper documents, electronic updates and evidence given at oral hearings.
Apply knowledge and judgement to offenders’ cases in order to decide whether they can safely be released into the community and to set conditions where release is appropriate.
Oversee the hearing of cases in order to assess risk.
Work collaboratively with other parole members in order to make judgements about the available evidence and to provide a concise and structured summary of relevant factors in reaching a decision or recommendation.
Facilitate report writing, draft reasoned summaries and decisions.
Be an effective ambassador for the Parole Board when representing it at hearings or any other event.
Facilitate administrative roles associated with preparation for hearings, hearings and revocations/cancellations, public education on parole, facilitate invitation of victims to hearings including court attendance as a result of litigation by offenders.
requirements:
A recognized and appropriate NQF level 7 qualification in any Criminal Justice field, Social Sciences or related.
Previous 5 years’ experience in management or decision-making position.
Demonstrable experience of and ability to conduct effective evidence-based decision making, weighing facts and evidence, analysing and critically evaluating large volumes of complex information and identifying key issues, within tight deadlines and working on your own initiative.
Demonstrable independence of mind and sound judgement, with the ability to make evidence-based decisions that are accurately documented.
Excellent interpersonal skills: The ability to gain respect and maintain rapport through effective communication and influencing skills - with the confidence to challenge opinions where necessary, work collegiately and resolve differences to reach sound decisions.
Excellent communication skills, both written and oral: The ability to communicate sensitively and effectively with a wide range of individuals, varying your approach as necessary and treating others with respect, to listen actively and evaluate replies in order to probe issues.
Excellent written skills: The ability to draft well-formed written reports which summarizes evidence in support of a decision or recommendation.
Demonstrable high standards of corporate and personal integrity and conduct, such as a strong commitment to fairness, equality and the ethos of supporting the wider public or community good through your contributions.
High levels of time management, organizational and administrative skills, together with strong personal motivation and commitment to professional self-development.
Evidence of experience of any aspect of the criminal justice system and an understanding of the importance of the victim’s perspective.
Previous experience in management or decision-making position.

Decision making in light of a number of factors, that is:- rights of the offender (as far as the right to be considered in light of relevant legislation), calculation of the minimum detention period, understanding of criminal justice value chain, court papers, sentencing remarks, copy of the judgment, copy of the warrant of detention, case law, SAP 69 and 62, understanding the various reports by the DCS professionals, understanding of the rehabilitation process, risk assessment, victim/community empathy, public safety etc. Applicants who have retired from the Public Service with a specific determination that they cannot be reappointed or have been declared medically unfit will not be considered. Term of office will be for a period of five (5) years or as may be determined by the Minister in line with Section 74 (7) of the Correctional Services Act, Act 111 of 1998. Applications: Applications must be submitted on the Z83 form (Public Service application form) accessible on the link below and must be completed in full. Only a detailed CV should be attached to your application form. Applicants must note that further checks will be conducted once they are shortlisted and that their appointment is subject to positive outcomes on these checks, which include security clearance, security vetting, qualification verification and criminal records verification. Candidates must comply with the minimum appointment requirements. CV’s should be aligned to reflect one’s degree of compliance with the advertisement requirements and responsibilities. about_role:
FirstRand is hiring a Transaction Manager, based in Johannesburg.
To support in the execution of and management of financial transactions adhering to regulatory compliance and defined policies and procedures.
To play a crucial role in ensuring accurate deal booking and adherence to established processes within the organisation’s Transaction Management function. Mitigate operational and reputational risk by validating the quality and accuracy of transaction data, ensuring alignment with regulatory requirements, and supporting effective risk management practices.
To collaborate with various stakeholders, including traders, risk management teams, and back-office processing functions, to uphold data integrity, streamline processes, and enhance the overall efficiency and accuracy of transaction management.
Conduct detailed reviews of transaction data to identify discrepancies, verify completeness, and ensure data integrity within transaction systems, thus supporting reliable financial reporting.
Engage in the due diligence process by compiling the necessary documentation and liaising with relevant advisors.
Act as a key point of contact, addressing inquiries, providing updates, and ensuring a high level of service throughout the transaction process to maintain client satisfaction and trust.
Monitor and ensure all transactions adhere to internal policies and external regulatory requirements, including KYC (Know Your Customer) and AML (Anti-Money Laundering) standards, to prevent legal and financial penalties.
Assist in the execution of transactions, coordinating closing logistics, finalising documentation, and ensuring all procedural requirements are met for successful transaction completion.
Validate that all transactions are booked accurately and in line with client instructions and regulatory requirements to minimise booking errors and reduce operational risk.
Identify and flags any inconsistencies or irregularities in transaction data, escalating issues promptly to mitigate financial and reputational risk.
Attend DCF's for all new deals and comment on Legal Agreements and ensure that the legal agreements can be operationalised.
Engage with the Deal Team and the TM to ensure that deal intention is understood and that Transaction Management can provide the support required to implement the deal and conduct the ongoing maintenance required.
Ensure processes are followed and backdate approval is required where necessary.
Ensure New Deal implementation is approved according to Legals and the DCF.
Reconcile transaction records across different systems to confirm data consistency and integrity across platforms.
Participate in projects aimed at improving transaction management processes, focusing on automation, accuracy, and efficiency to enhance data quality standards.
Communicate transaction data quality insights to internal stakeholders, including traders and risk managers, ensuring transparency and promoting proactive issue resolution.
Develop and monitor key metrics for data quality within the transaction management function, ensuring consistent and quantifiable improvement.
Identify and implement process improvements to enhance efficiency, accuracy, and client service in transaction management data quality, contributing to operational excellence.
Track and report on transaction-related risks, collaborating with senior managers to develop and implement effective risk mitigation strategies.
Collaborate with internal teams i.e., legal, compliance, credit, and operations to ensure cohesive and efficient transaction management.
Engage in ongoing training and development activities to build expertise in transaction management
Build and sustain collaborative working relationships with relevant peers and stakeholders to achieve productivity synergies.
Participate in specialist communities of practice and contribute positively to own and organisational knowledge improvement.

Achievement of departmental sales targets.

Experience managing and developing teams in a retail environment.

job_title: Senior Credit Manager, Natural Resources, Origination, CIB
about_role:
Standard Bank is hiring a Senior Credit Manager, Natural Resources, Origination, CIB, based in Johannesburg, Gauteng.
To provide independent credit risk leadership and transaction support for Natural Resources financing opportunities across South Africa and the broader African continent. The role works closely with Coverage, Product and Transaction teams during the origination, structuring and execution of transactions to ensure that key risks are identified early, properly assessed and appropriately mitigated.
The incumbent will play an important role in shaping transactions before formal credit submission by providing clear risk insight, challenging proposed structures and assumptions, and influencing outcomes that are aligned with the Bank’s risk appetite and strategic objectives. The role requires close engagement with internal and external stakeholders, including clients, sponsors, advisers and transaction teams, to support sustainable financing solutions while preserving credit quality and portfolio integrity.
As a subject matter expert within Natural Resources, the incumbent will provide informed credit input on sector trends, emerging risks, commodity markets, operating environments and industry developments across the relevant geographies. The role is expected to support high-quality credit decision-making through robust analysis, sound judgement and well-reasoned recommendations that ensure transactions are appropriately structured and capable of delivering acceptable risk-adjusted returns. This includes the review of term sheets, legal agreements, security and transaction documents to ensure risks are appropriately identified, mitigated and documented.
This role works closely with Environmental, Governance and Social Risk advisory to identify and assess ESG risks associated with transactions and ensure alignment with Bank policy, sector appetite and sustainability objectives.
The incumbent will lead the presentation and discussion of transactions at Credit Committees and other senior approval forums, providing clear recommendations supported by robust analysis and balanced risk assessment.
In this role the incumbent will originate credit applications for new transactions and when necessary, prepare or evaluate annual review credit applications, ensuring transactions remain aligned with the Bank's risk appetite, policy requirements and strategic objectives. The incumbent to provide coaching, technical guidance and leadership to less experienced credit professionals, contributing to capability development across the Natural Resources credit team.
Success in the role will be measured by the quality of credit risk assessment, the strength of risk challenge, the ability to influence transaction outcomes, and the contribution made to growing a sustainable, well-managed and resilient Natural Resources credit portfolio.
requirements:
Professional Qualifications:
Preference will be given to candidates holding a CA(SA), CFA, FRM, or other relevant professional qualification demonstrating advanced expertise in financial analysis, risk assessment, and transaction evaluation.
Type of Qualification: Post Graduate Degree
Field of Study: Business Commerce, Finance, Accounting, Economics, Engineering, Mathematics, or a related discipline.
Experience Required:
8 to 10 years’ experience in credit risk, preferably with meaningful exposure to the Natural Resources sector, including mining and metals, oil and gas, or related sectors. A strong track record of working on new, complex and structured transactions across South Africa and the broader African continent is required. Experience in project finance, corporate lending, global market derivative products, leveraged finance, trade finance, or diversified industrials would be advantageous.
Well-developed knowledge of financial markets, commodity markets, macroeconomic trends, and the regional geographies in which the portfolio operates. The incumbent should be able to assess sector developments, country-specific risks, technical feasibility and transaction-level risks in a manner that supports sound credit decision-making.
Thorough conceptual and practical knowledge of credit procedures, credit policies, delegated authority frameworks, credit rating methodologies, Basel requirements, regulatory expectations, and compliance standards. Strong understanding of banking products and facilities that give rise to counterparty credit risk is required.

about_role:
Standard Bank is hiring an Entrenchment Universal Banker, based in Gqeberha, Eastern Cape.
To drive sales growth and deepen client relationships in Personal and Private Banking through proactive outbound and inbound telesales and virtual client engagement (calls, chat and email). The role converts sales opportunities into the right solutions, achieves set sales and cross-sell targets, and delivers on entrenchment Key Performance Indicators such as activation, onboarding and retention.
responsibilities:
Sell and cross-sell Personal and Private Banking products through outbound and inbound telesales, taking ownership of individual sales targets and Key Performance Indicators.
Run outbound sales and entrenchment campaigns and convert inbound enquiries into sales, delivering uplift in transactional activity, cross-sell and retention.
Hold needs-based sales conversations that identify client needs, recommend the right solution and secure the sale.
Explain product features, benefits, pricing and conditions clearly, and educate clients on self-service, Interactive Voice Response and their rights and obligations in line with the Code of Banking Practice.
Accurately capture applications and daily activity on the required tools, and adhere to all risk, compliance and Financial Advisory and Intermediary Services Act requirements.
requirements:
Minimum experience:
Minimum of 2 to 3 years’ total experience in a call centre environment, with a good understanding of bank processes, policies and products.
Experience as an Outbound Sales Consultant or in a similar target-driven telesales role, preferably within banking, insurance or funeral policy sales.
Experience engaging clients telephonically, identifying sales opportunities and promoting products and services across outbound and inbound calls.
Proven ability to achieve sales targets, handle objections and convert client conversations into successful sales.
Experience working with sales targets, conversion rates, client relationship management systems and sales reporting.
National Certificate in Banking (NQF 5), FAIS-recognised, or an equivalent relevant qualification.
Must meet the applicable FAIS Fit and Proper requirements for the role.
Behavioural competencies:
Convincing People
Pursuing Goals
Establishing Rapport
Meeting Timescales
Following Procedures
Upholding Standards
Technical competencies:
Outbound and Inbound Telesales
Needs-Based Selling and Cross-Sell
Objection Handling and Closing
Banking, Insurance and Funeral Product Knowledge
Risk, Compliance and Regulatory Governance
Sales Performance and Client Relationship Management Systems
